review: A really great reimagining of an early internet flash game. I remember playing a long time ago, and while it is as intriguing and entertaining as it was back in 2009, there are some things I wish they kept. For one, the original Voice actors are just much better. And two, while the music is enjoyable in this game, that old Morningstar background music really sets the atmosphere for this small point and click adventure. You are missing the sauce, even with the additional story and animations. Sorry to say.

I loved this game when it was free on Kongregate. So when I was watching a streamer and the beginning scene started I was like "hey this looks familiar" and immediately stopped the video so I could see if I could replay it. In short, nostalgia made me get it and I had just as much fun replaying it as when I first found the game years ago. I didn't encounter any bugs this time, but I do remember having a few when it was on kongregate, so just a heads up on that. also the voice acting is a little awkward but it just gives it more charm in my opinion.

Un jeu d'aventure spatiale super captivant avec une superbe ambiance !
Notre vaisseau se crache sur une planète hostile, et nous devons trouver un moyen de nous en échapper.
Recherches, exploration, découvertes, voici ce qui nous attend.
Les dessins sont beaux, les énigmes logiques et la progression se fait au fur et à mesure des découvertes.
Un excellent jeu de 2 à 3 heures.
Des succès Steam liés à l'histoire (2 ou 3 peuvent être ratés)

I remember when this was just a quaint little flash game, and now seeing it on Steam is like a proud proud parent seeing their kid graduate(after learning about it 10 years later...)! I couldn't be happier to play it again, and seeing it have some new bells and whistles attached was a pleasant and welcome surprise on top of that! 

While not particularly long(especially if you've already played it long ago) nor overly complicated like some point-and-clicks can be, Morningstar is like a tall glass of cool water going down a sore throat: it may go down quick, but that time is smooth and refreshing. The game is pretty straightforward in its gameplay and puzzle-solving, and I doubt you'll find yourself getting lost with what to do next as those steps are pretty well telegraphed with each piece of the puzzle you pick up throughout. 

The strongest point of the game has to be the creative worldbuilding, which has stuck with me the most after all this time. What the game does explore with the world and its circumstances will leave you with questions, but also plenty of interpretable answers for you to fill in the gaps with yourself. It's a creative sci-fi environment they've built here, one they should be proud of! 

Overall, this game is a nostalgic blast from the past that was well worth my money, and it'll be well worth yours no matter how much time it takes to finish it. I will be watching for any future works with great interest!

Simple and short point and click adventure. Smooth interface, no pixelhunt needed.

Morningstar: Descent to Deadrock is a point and click mini-adventure game. You collect objects, combine objects,  interact with environment to solve the situation you are in. There is no time, reflex concerned mini games or such, pure point and click. I added "mini" because it's really short game you can finish it in 1 sitting.  It took me like 2-3 hrs. 

+Story/Setting : You crash land on an uncharted planet. You need to get out and unravel some mystery. Sounds familiar right? Yes, but well executed so it's ok. 

+Gameplay: It's simple point and click, most of the time solutions make sense or obvious. Unlike many point and click games you don't wait your character to go to some place, you always have a scene and discover interesting points by moving your mouse. It's easy but fun.
Only downside I can think of the voice acting, it's overly cheesy regarding the situation the character is in.

-Technical: I happen to have a small bug where you can't select some objects, just quit and re entering the  game fixes it. It really takes 15 seconds anyway. 

Good buy on a sale.

This short point and click game appeared on Steam 10 years ago and still holds up well.  I believe it was a flash game in a previous life.
You play Powell travelling on the merchant ship Morningstar when you are unexpectantly pulled in by the gravity of an alien planet and crash.  One person is killed, the captain badly injured and you are the only person who can save the day.  Exploration outside the ship shows the remains of another larger ship with no survivors.  Slowly you unravel what happened to them...and it is not pretty.
The story arc was good and builds up plenty of intrigue, but all your questions won't be resolved at the end. 
Voiceovers were excellent.  I loved the wordplay between Powell and the captain....their interaction made their characters very believable.  You actually realise that one of them isn't particularly nice.  If you need hints, click the radio and the captain's voice tells you what you need to do.
Gameplay is pretty straightforward and hotspots show what to interact with.  You get quite a few objects in your inventory.  You have to be innovative and combine objects together to create functional systems.  I fell down in this area and had to look up a guide now and then.
Graphics are adequate as this is a re-mastered version.  Cutscenes are good, but don't expect state of the art graphics.  I quite liked the muted tones of the game.
If you like sci-fi vibes and space themes and don't mind a short game, this is for you.  Wait for a sale though.

Things that bothered me a bit : navigation, the voice overs, the dialogue, missing subtitles during the end movie.

The puzzles where mostly of the type 'find something' and 'figure out where to use it'. The other type of puzzle was to figure out an alien language. In itself an interesting concept, but the execution could perhaps have been clearer. I also didn't realize that not all keys on the keypad did the same thing.
For perhaps half of all puzzles I had to use a walkthrough, because, even with the captain telling me what to do, I couldn't figure it out ...

Clearing out my backlog, this P&C adventure game really shows its age with poor fast-travel, a horrendous inventory system (so glad I picked up that fish on the second screen that serves no purpose except cluttering up my inventory; I get the joke but it's still irritating) and highlights based on mouse-overs that lead to you wildly swooping over every room to make sure you don't miss something.

All that and an incredibly obtuse puzzle at the very end that explains what it wants but not how to do it (do you enter the "off" symbols before or after the thing you want turned on/off?).

But all could be forgiven if the writing and VA is good. Reader, it is not. We get two people who are not friends, are in fact openly antagonistic, unprofessional and above all seem irritated that they are even here. It's a bold directoral choice for two astronauts who are professionals selected to travel to interstellar destinations. The main character, Powell, is a particular lowlight, someone who seems to hate that he is even here today - but without any of the charm or surprise of a Han Solo type.

At least it's short.

It also left some questions and curiosity about the worlds and history that it glimpsed us.

It also had some hand holding mechanics to help guide you in the right direction, not leave an area unless you had everything you needed and you can radio a crew member for a "hint" which made for a bit more of an immersive way of getting a hint. 

I have never made a game and appreciate what it takes to do so as well as the story telling and intention of it all.  I thought this was well done in the intention with some silliness and humour of those who made it mixed in. Visually well done and the Voice work fit in with it all. 

Control wise it worked well for what was needed in game.  Only once did I completely miss seeing something of importance, in which case the RADIO hint eventually got me to see it!

It has the feel that it was been made by one person, or some friends.

An great remake of an old flash game. Same premise - crash landed, escape, point and click - but has a few improvements:
* Much better cutscenes.
* Some interactions are animated which adds a bit of immersion to the experience
* The end-game is greatly expanded on from the original story with a few more puzzles and an amended story.
* Slightly improved voice acting (which depending on where you played the original, wasn't included at all).
* Improved aesthetic through focus on lighting, (marginally) better textures, and much better models.
* Some puzzles have been changed to make them much easier to follow.
* New object highlight icons that help to remember where things are.

Muita nostalgia. Finalizava esse jogo de tempos em tempos enquanto era pirralho ainda no tempo que ele era um joguinho flash da Kongregate. Fui procurar ele pra jogar de novo recentemente só pra matar a nostalgia e a versão flash na Kongregate não funciona mais nem com o Supernova (que é o "emulador" de flash usado pelo site atualmente). Tive muita sorte de achar ele aqui na Steam. Uma grande oportunidade de recompensar os desenvolvedores pela diversão que me proporcionaram na infância.
É bom mencionar que esse jogo não é de 2015. Ele foi na verdade lançado em 2009, e como mencionei era um game flash. Era um jogo de browser gratuito, feito por uma galera unicamente para entreter, não pra lucrar alguma coisa em cima do jogo. É bom levar tudo isso em consideração na hora de avaliar.

Naquela época o mundo Sci-fi ainda era algo extremamente novo e espetacular para mim e esse foi o primeiro jogo que eu joguei que apresentou a proposta de ter de escapar de um planeta deserto, cheio de perigos e mistérios. Para uma criança ou adolescente a complexidade da história e o nível de dublagem serão suficientes para deixá-lo entretido, e a duração do jogo também não será um problema porque não é todo pirralho que iria curtir passar 5 ou 6 horas tentando desvendar os puzzles de um jogo point-n-click. Eu mesmo já apelava para os walkthroughs quando o jogo point-n-click estava sendo longo demais. Os gráficos para meu eu da época eram fantásticos, ainda mais para um jogo de browser gratuito.
Aqui na versão da Steam eu não enfrentei bugs, crashes nem nada do tipo enquanto jogava ele. A qualidade das cutscenes está ótima também, e muito melhor do que na versão flash.
Porém, sei que hoje em dia os jogos point-n-click não são mais tão atrativos para o público para o qual o jogo é voltado, e esse é o único problema. Isso junto aos gráficos antigos dificultam que o jogo ganhe destaque com as novas gerações de jogadores, e o público adulto que for jogar esse jogo pela primeira vez não ficará muito satisfeito, pois o jogo não foi lançado voltado para o público adulto. 
Ainda assim para quem o jogou na infância, como eu, é uma ótima opçao se quiser um pouco de nostalgia.

[h1]*Morningstar: Descent to Deadrock* - Ein kleines Sci-Fi-Abenteuer[/h1]

Nach einem unerklärlichen Absturz mit unserem Shuttle finden wir uns auf einem scheinbar unbewohnten Planeten wieder. Um unser Raumschiff wieder flott zu bekommen, bedarf es einiges an Improvisation und wir kommen nicht umhin, dabei auch den Planeten zu erkunden und hinter das Geheimnis unseres Absturzes zu kommen.

Ein schön gemachtes Sci-Fi-Abenteuer mit vielen abwechslungsreichen Rätseln, die nicht immer leicht zu lösen sind (wir müssen schließlich mit dem Wenigen was wir finden können improvisieren). Kommen wir hierbei mal nicht weiter, können wir über Funk unseren verletzten Captain im Cockpit fragen. Er fungiert als implementiertes Hilfesystem im Spiel und ist für so manchen verbalen Schlagabtausch zu haben.

Mir hat das Spiel wirklich sehr viel Spaß gemacht und es hat mir gut gefallen, wie sich die Story entwickelt. Allerdings sollte man nicht zu viel erwarten. Das Spiel ist sehr kurz und kann natürlich mit anderen Vertretern des Genres nicht mithalten. Daher finde ich den Vollpreis auch zu hoch angesetzt.

Zum Schluss sei noch gesagt, dass alle Achievements in einem Durchgang machbar sind und bei gründlichem Absuchen nicht verpasst werden können.

Mir hat das Spiel gut gefallen. Im Sale kann ich es deshalb auf jeden Fall weiterempfehlen.
